text:
maria: heads-up: customer reported a spike of 502s on Hosted API around 09:12 UTC. All failures correlate with requests that include a very large billing metadata header (X-Billing-Meta). 10 occurrences across 3 tenants in the last 30m. Can infra triage?

sam: saw one of the failed requests. curl shows 502 and nginx upstream reset. quick repro: `curl -v -H \"X-Billing-Meta: \$(python -c 'print(\"A\"*70000)')\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d @small.json` -> 502.

ingress-bot: nginx error snippet from node ngx-123: `2026/03/18 09:14:23 [crit] 1024#0: *4567 writev() failed (12: Cannot allocate memory) while sending to client, client: 10.8.2.45, server: _, request: \"POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/2\", upstream: \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/\"`

aj: checked kernel logs on the same host: `Out of memory: Kill process 1024 (nginx) score 987 or sacrifice child` and OOM killed one nginx worker right after the 502s. So large header seems to be causing buffer allocation spike in NGINX worker.

katie: likely NGINX buffers + proxying large header -> worker tries to allocate proxy buffers per request and gets OOM under burst. Envoy upstream would see connection reset -> 502 returned. Also check NGINX config for `large_client_header_buffers` + `proxy_buffer_size` values.

sam: quick triage in staging: bumping `large_client_header_buffers 4 16k` -> still repro at ~70KB header. Need `large_client_header_buffers 4 64k` to avoid NGINX rejecting the header and instead passing upstream. But that only shifts memory pressure.

aj: long-term we shouldn't let arbitrary billing metadata grow that large. Two immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce header size limit at frontdoor and return 413/400; 2) strip X-Billing-Meta at edge and pass a truncated id downstream.

maria: customer SDK is sending full invoice blobs in header (bad). We should coordinate a communication asking them to move payload into request body or S3 and send reference id.

ingress-bot: sample repro logs (full):
```
2026/03/18 09:13:58 [error] 1024#0: *4500 recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer) while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: _, request: \"POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/2\", upstream: \"http://127.0.0.1:8080/\", host: \"api.redwood.ai\"
2026/03/18 09:13:58 [crit] 1024#0: *4500 writev() failed (12: Cannot allocate memory) while sending to client
kernel: [  123.456789] nginx[1024]: segfault or killed by OOM
```

sam: quick mitigation plan I can run now: 1) deploy a Lua rewrite to drop/truncate X-Billing-Meta at the edge for requests > 8KB; 2) add a per-node guard: `limit_conn` lane? probably not; 3) start a small canary increase of `large_client_header_buffers` + monitor memory.

katie: also consider Envoy settings for private deployments: `max_request_headers_kb` -> default 96 KB in some configs, but our frontdoor (NGINX) is the choke point. If we increase NGINX buffers, we must also ensure we don't let worker memory blow up on high concurrency. Use `worker_connections`/`worker_rlimit` and per-request accounting.

aj: added quick kernel-level check: on the affected host concurrent ephemeral memory usage peaked when 6 concurrent large-header requests arrived. So increasing buffer sizes will only work if concurrency is low.

deploy-bot: started canary patch: ingress-lua-trim-xbilling @ 10% traffic -> `started` (deploy 5 of 50).

sam: after canary started, error-rate for that customer dropped to near 0 within 2 minutes. Reproduced locally: when header is trimmed we get 200/streaming responses normal.

maria: customer informed and moved to using body/s3 ref. They saw immediate improvement. Closing short-term incident.

katie: follow-ups: - (action) eng-infra to add header-size enforcement rule at frontdoor (config + docs) - (action) product -> update SDK to detect/warn large billing header - (action) support -> notify customers about header size policy and best practice (use body or references)

maria: thanks everyone. Saving logs and repro steps to support ticket #S-4321. We'll schedule infra follow-up next week. :thumbsup:
